summary.intent: Use the GSD (Get Stuff Done) workflow system to plan and then execute Phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) of the cipher-box project, and in parallel set up an independent worktree to begin Phase 69 (Rust/FUSE/WinFsp) planning.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning completed end-to-end (research, Nyquist validation, pattern mapping, 12 plans across 7 waves, plan-checker PASSED, coverage gates satisfied) and committed; execution proceeded sequentially through Wave 4 plan 04 (5/12 plans done, all green) with a quota-driven pause/resume handled via ScheduleWakeup; a separate git worktree for Phase 69 was created off origin/main for independent parallel work.

repo: GSD `gsd-tools query commit` has a known false-negative: it can report `commit_failed` even though the commit verifiably lands in git log (confirmed multiple times this session, matches prior memory).
In this pnpm monorepo, web-package executors must rebuild the SDK dist before typecheck when SDK exports change mid-phase — a cross-package staleness landmine.

Worktree-based parallel executors each need their own `pnpm install`, which is expensive; for phases with mostly single-plan waves, sequential execution on the main tree is faster and equally correct when the planner made same-wave plans file-disjoint.

`worktree.baseRef` config can be `head` (fork from live HEAD) vs a `fresh` default (fork from origin/main) — must be checked before dispatching worktree executors, since forking from origin/main would omit uncommitted-to-main PLAN.md files.

Multiple plan executors in a phase can prematurely mark shared REQUIREMENTS.md checkboxes `[x]` before all requirement-spanning plans actually complete (seen with SDK-READ-01/02/03/04) — needs manual orchestrator correction back to `[ ]` until the true completion plan lands.
The gap-analysis post-planning check's JSON `rendered` field can contain control characters that break naive parsing; running the check directly bypasses this.

Phase 68.2's D-07 scope decision (full-boundary grep gate covering BYO-pinning settings and auth-bootstrap/device-registry crypto, not just folder-listing paths) was a genuine ambiguity the researcher surfaced and required a user decision, then was locked into CONTEXT.md before planning.

code.finding: ROT-07 anti-rollback gate (RotationHighWater.enforceResolved) added to root resolve path (resolvePublishedNode) in plan 68.2-01.
enforceResolved gate also added to dfsFindFolder child-loop read path in plan 68.2-01, alongside pre-existing write-path gate at line 1156.

resolveChildren docstring documents that per-child resolve/unseal failures are skipped (graceful degradation) rather than propagated, because the parent folder is already gated via ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder before this runs — an unverifiable sibling is omitted, never rendered with stale/attacker content, and the trust boundary holds since navigating into any child re-triggers the gate.

workflow: When scheduling a wake-up (ScheduleWakeup) after computing a target time, recompute delaySeconds from the actual current time immediately before the call — a stale timestamp (from before a quota interruption) caused a miscalculated wake (04:35 instead of the intended 4:10am).

For independent, unrelated work streams (different phase, different subsystem), creating a separate `git worktree add` off origin/main lets you parallelize without disturbing the main checkout's in-progress branch/execution.

When a background executor reports a deviation from plan (e.g., widened error handling), spot-check by reading the actual changed code and re-running the specific security-relevant tests independently rather than trusting the self-report, especially for security-critical read-path code.

friction: Session hit its quota/session limit mid-execution (between Wave 4 plan 04 finishing and the ScheduleWakeup call), forcing an ad hoc pause/resume flow.
First ScheduleWakeup attempt was miscalculated (targeted 04:35 instead of 4:10am) because the delay was computed off a pre-quota-gap timestamp; had to be corrected with a second call.

`git fetch` failed with no network access from the sandboxed session, requiring reliance on a locally cached origin/main ref (verified as current only by cross-checking it matched the fork-base of the active branch).
The post-planning gap-analysis check's JSON output had control characters that broke the parser, requiring a direct re-run of the check instead.

Executors repeatedly mis-marked shared REQUIREMENTS.md checkboxes as complete before their true completion plan landed, requiring manual detection and correction by the orchestrator across multiple waves.
A stray/duplicate ScheduleWakeup (04:11) could not be cleanly retracted after the user said to just keep going without waiting; had to be treated as a harmless future no-op.
